correctness.rationale: All posterior normalizations are positive. Relative to the common base measure, the ratio for indices i<j is a positive constant times (u/(1-u))^(j-i) on (0,1); the atom at 0 can only add to the lower-index posterior and the atom at 1 can only add to the higher-index posterior. The one crossing gives both stochastic order and TV equal to the maximum CDF gap. The endpoint CDF gap dominates every posterior gap; expanding a pair of mixed rows as a convex combination of posterior differences bounds its TV by the endpoint TV, which the rows at 0 and 1 attain. Equality in the endpoint densities gives the stated theta, and an atom at theta contributes zero. Positive overlap on the interior gives TV<1, including the possible zero case. Regularity of finite Borel measures gives continuous [0,1]-valued approximations of the maximizing indicator in the two endpoint integrals, proving the oscillation supremum. The symmetric joint kernel gives stationarity; Jordan decomposition gives the TV bound, sharp for the two endpoint point masses in one step. The uniform integral is 1-2^(-n).
residual_risks: The supplied finite checks are not an all-measure proof or a formal certificate; no sharp coefficient for powers is claimed.

value.rationale: The retained difference from the exact Jacobi result is a routine extension of its proof, not a new sharp estimate requiring any new idea for singular measures. In the old proof replace the Lebesgue densities of posterior beta laws by the posterior Radon–Nikodym densities b_(n,k)/Z_k relative to the common base measure. In the likelihood ratio the base cancels; the same odds powers give the same two-by-two minor signs, CDF ordering, and endpoint sandwich, without beta integrals. The polynomial minors extend to u=0 and u=1 by continuity independent of whether the base charges those points; regularity handles the continuous test functions. The new threshold only substitutes the generalized normalizers. Neither the uniform formula nor a new singular-base asymptotic, extremal phenomenon, or contraction calculation remains as a distinct substantive result. The class of arbitrary bases is natural, but the exact invariant transfers mechanically from the closest proof.
residual_risks: This judgment is about the contribution made here, not about whether arbitrary-measure Bernstein–Durrmeyer operators are worth studying.
